input.text: In Colorado branches, customers may request a fee refund within 30 days of the statement date.
input.heading: Colorado requirements

input.text: In Kansas branches, retain closed account records for 5 years from the closing date.
input.heading: Kansas requirements

input.text: In Oklahoma branches, resolve complaints within 30 business days of receipt, or tell the customer when to expect a resolution.
input.heading: Oklahoma requirements

input.text: In Texas branches, mail the customer a notice at least 45 days before the account is classified as dormant.
input.heading: Texas requirements

input.text: Accounts open fewer than 90 days are new accounts for hold and limit purposes.
input.heading: What branches need to know

document.title: Branch Bulletin 2025-34: How long an account counts as new
document.applies_to: All branches. Consumer and small business accounts.

input.text: A teller drawer may not hold more than $10,000 at any time.
input.heading: What branches need to know

document.title: Branch Bulletin 2025-04: Teller drawer cash limit

input.text: Disputes over $250 are reviewed by a card services specialist before credit is issued.
input.heading: What branches need to know

document.title: Branch Bulletin 2026-18: Dispute amount that needs card services review
document.applies_to: All branches. Consumer and small business accounts.

input.text: Regional managers may approve rate exceptions of up to 0.75%.
input.heading: What branches need to know

document.title: Branch Bulletin 2025-16: Regional manager rate exception limit

input.text: An operations manager must give a second approval for any outgoing wire above $50,000.
input.heading: Steps to follow

document.title: Branch Bulletin 2025-24: Callback threshold for outgoing wires

input.text: Complaints that allege unfair treatment are escalated to the branch manager the same day.
input.heading: Who handles a complaint that alleges unfair treatment?
